title: Optional Properties and Parameters knowledge check

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of a precise TypeScript type?
options: To express the intended values and let the compiler detect incompatible uses.
To convert or sanitize an external value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: To express the intended values and let the compiler detect incompatible uses.
questions.explanation: Types describe expected program values but do not automatically change or validate runtime data.

questions.prompt: Which statement is correct about “Optional Properties and Parameters”?
options: The learner should publish hidden solutions so the exercise can grade itself.
The concept should be demonstrated with the ? modifier and checked against its intended contract.
The safest approach is to skip diagnostics and trust the first output.
A type assertion automatically validates every value at runtime.
questions.answer_key: The concept should be demonstrated with the ? modifier and checked against its intended contract.
questions.explanation: The supplied syllabus explicitly includes “The ? modifier”; connect it to a concrete example and verify the behavior relevant to this lesson.

questions.prompt: What is a good verification step after practicing “Optional Properties and Parameters”?
options: Check optional properties in objects, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
Assume the distinction between absence and explicit undefined is unnecessary because the code has type annotations.
Ignore compiler or test failures if the interface looks correct.
Treat passing a static token check as proof that the program executed correctly.
questions.answer_key: Check optional properties in objects, include a meaningful failure case where appropriate, and document any runtime or version assumptions.
questions.explanation: The syllabus includes “Optional properties in objects”. Verification should match the concept: type-level checks, runtime tests, configuration checks or human review as appropriate.
